title: Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
authors: Federico Finkel, Artemio González-López, Martín Zapata
abstract: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.
summary: This paper develops a discrete WKB method to calculate local particle densities in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains, specifically using the Rice-Mele model relevant to optical superlattices. It rigorously demonstrates that the WKB results match the Local Density Approximation (LDA) predictions. This provides crucial theoretical tools for understanding how quantum properties manifest in engineered, spatially varying quantum materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to derive explicit semiclassical expressions for local observables, such as particle density, in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains.
main_result: The discrete WKB density profiles are shown to agree with those obtained from the Local Density Approximation (LDA), providing analytic expressions for sublattice-resolved particle densities.
method: The authors extend the discrete WKB method to matrix difference equations, analyzing the classical action integral along the allowed energy bands.
model_or_system: The system is an inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chain, specifically modeled after the Rice-Mele (RM) model, which is proposed for realization in optical superlattices using ultracold atoms.
key_observables: Single-particle wave functions, density of states, sublattice-resolved local particle densities, and the filling fraction at an arbitrary Fermi energy.
important_parameters: The slowly varying nature of the hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials, and the Fermi energy ($\epsilon_F$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes slowly varying potentials, allowing the use of the WKB approximation, and relies on the LDA to connect local observables to homogeneous results.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis involves visualizing the two branches of the classical trajectory $\Gamma_j(\epsilon)$ and the resulting density profiles across different filling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the Hamiltonian (Section 2), analyzing the homogeneous spectrum (Section 3), deriving the LDA (Section 4), applying the WKB treatment (Section 5), calculating density/DOS (Section 6), and concluding with illustrative examples (Section 7).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the theoretical description of quantum systems realized in optical lattices (a core AMO platform), providing semiclassical tools to calculate bulk properties like density profiles in spatially varying potentials.
